USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Phase I reaction

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A hepatic enzyme converts a drug into a more polar metabolite by adding oxygen to the molecule. No glucuronic acid, sulfate or other conjugating group is attached. Which classification best describes this biotransformation reaction?

  1. Unchanged renal excretion
  2. Plasma-protein binding
  3. Phase I oxidation
  4. Phase II glucuronidation
  5. Phase II sulfation
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Phase I oxidation

Oxidation is a phase I functionalization reaction.

Understanding the options

Phase I oxidation
Oxidation is a phase I functionalization reaction.
Phase II glucuronidation
No glucuronic acid is attached.
Phase II sulfation
No sulfate conjugate is formed.
Unchanged renal excretion
The molecule is chemically altered in the liver.
Plasma-protein binding
Binding is not the described chemical transformation.
